bibl.title: Operant Conditioning of H-Reflex Can Correct a Locomotor Abnormality after Spinal Cord Injury in Rats

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether operant conditioning of a spinal reflex can change locomotion after spinal cord injury
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether descending input shaped by reflex conditioning can improve motor function in the injured spinal cord
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: shows a targeted reflex conditioning protocol removes a lesion-induced locomotor asymmetry, establishing the principle that descending-input conditioning can change a complex motor behaviour
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: H-reflex operant conditioning after spinal cord injury
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Up-conditioning strengthens the motoneuron response to primary afferent input, recruiting more motoneurons into the locomotor burst (and making each fire more), which enlarges and broadens the soleus burst and thereby lengthens right stance until symmetry is restored
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The enlarged locomotor burst produced by up-conditioning is the proposed origin of the restored right/left symmetry
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: In normal animals compensatory adjustments by other muscles cancel the conditioning-induced change; in lesioned animals those compensatory adjustments are impaired or absent, so the conditioning effect is allowed to alter locomotion
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: up-conditioning raises the locomotor burst, probably by recruiting more motoneurons to primary afferent input, and the burst also broadens
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the lesion spares the corticospinal tract, which is the only descending path known to be essential for H-reflex conditioning - so the protocol can still work
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: in intact animals other muscles compensate and symmetry is preserved; after injury that compensation is impaired, so the same conditioning changes locomotion
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conditioning is delivered continuously in the home cage, 3000-9000 stimulus trials per day over 50 days
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: H-reflex size is expressed in units of background EMG rather than peak-to-peak, because the rat H-reflex form is too variable for a peak measure
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The study only establishes the principle; the functional and clinical significance of the effect is not yet assessed.
span.note: what this limits: what the study establishes, stated by the authors as principle only: THE PRESENT RESULTS MERELY VALIDATE THE PRINCIPLE THAT SPINAL REFLEX CONDITIONING CAN AFFECT A COMPLEX MOTOR FUNCTION AFTER SPINAL CORD INJURY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Whether treadmill results in quadrupedal rats transfer to over-ground walking in bipedal humans is unknown.
span.note: what this limits: transfer to human walking: THE EXTENT TO WHICH THE EFFECTS OF CONDITIONING ON TREADMILL LOCOMOTION IN THE QUADRIPEDAL RAT PREDICT ITS EFFECTS ON OVER-GROUND LOCOMOTION IN THE BIPEDAL HUMAN REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: How long the conditioning effects last is not established.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about how long the effect lasts: THE LONG-TERM PERSISTENCE OF THE EFFECTS OF H-REFLEX CONDITIONING IS NOT YET WELL DEFINED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Large between-rat variability in absolute EMG measures limits the power to detect group differences.
span.note: what this limits: between-group comparisons on absolute measures: THIS WIDE INTER-RAT VARIABILITY MEANS THAT VERY LARGE GROUPS OF LC AND NORMAL RATS WOULD BE NEEDED FOR INTERGROUP DIFFERENCES TO BECOME SIGNIFICANT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the measured asymmetry is an EMG proxy, and whether it corresponds to an actual limp is stated to be unknown
span.note: what this limits: the step from the EMG measure to the behaviour: IT IS NOT AS YET CLEAR WHETHER THE SOLEUS EMG ASYMMETRY CREATED BY THE LC LESION IS ASSOCIATED WITH AN ACTUAL LIMP IN WALKING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the results are said to merely validate a principle, with clinical significance unassessed
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the principle, not the clinical application: MUCH REMAINS TO BE LEARNED BEFORE THE POTENTIAL of the method is known
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: only soleus bursts were measured; stance and swing need direct measurement and other muscles are untested
span.note: what this limits: the soleus-burst proxy for stance and swing: THE DATA PRESENTED HERE RELY ON THE RIGHT AND LEFT SOLEUS LOCOMOTOR BURSTS TO ASSESS SPECIFIC ASPECTS OF LOCOMOTION, and these measures only APPEAR TO PARALLEL THE RIGHT AND LEFT STANCE PHASES OF LOCOMOTION
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether quadrupedal treadmill results predict bipedal over-ground human locomotion is undetermined
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[1] · what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - prediction from quadrupedal treadmill work to BIPEDAL HUMAN over-ground locomotion
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the long-term persistence of the effect is not well defined, and up-conditioning decays faster than down-conditioning in monkeys
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - persistence, where the human comparison is that THE EFFECTS OF DOWN-CONDITIONING ARE STILL EVIDENT 4 MONTHS LATER
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: inter-rat variability in absolute EMG measures is so wide that very large groups would be needed for group differences to reach significance
span.note: what this limits: absolute measures specifically: ABSOLUTE MEASURES SUCH AS SOLEUS BURST AMPLITUDE DIFFER WIDELY ACROSS NORMAL RATS AND EVEN BETWEEN THE RIGHT AND LEFT LEGS OF INDIVIDUAL RATS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the locomotor analysis uses only the seven rats in which conditioning succeeded
span.note: what this limits: the up-conditioning locomotion analysis, which used only the animals in which conditioning worked: THE SEVEN SUCCESSFUL RATS CONSTITUTED THE EXPERIMENTAL GROUP OF HRup RATS FOR EVALUATION OF THE EFFECTS OF UP-CONDITIONING ON TREADMILL LOCOMOTION
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: 13 female rats only
span.note: what this limits: any sex-general reading: SUBJECTS WERE 13 FEMALE SPRAGUE DAWLEY RATS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reward-contingent shaping, applied to a spinal reflex rather than to a voluntary action
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: evidence that far fewer trials suffice in people, used to argue the rat protocol's intensity is not a barrier
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: five rats that were never exposed to up-conditioning, run through the same two sessions as the conditioned animals
span.note: eliminates: the passage of time and repeated testing as the explanation of the change - if the unconditioned rats changed too, the effect would not be the conditioning · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: locomotor abnormality here means an EMG burst-onset asymmetry, not an observed gait defect - the paper says whether there is a limp at all is unknown
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: successful conditioning is stipulated as a change of at least 20% in the intended direction, a criterion carried over from earlier papers
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the abnormality is PHYSIOLOGICALLY defined and the lesion ANATOMICALLY defined - the paper states the two bases separately
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: symmetry is an index constructed so that 0.5 means symmetric, built from burst-onset times rather than from limb kinematics
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · H-reflex —operationalised-as→ background EMG
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span explained why the measure is used. This sentence IS THE OPERATIONALISATION, as a formula: 'H-reflex size was calculated as average EMG amplitude in the H-reflex interval MINUS AVERAGE BACKGROUND EMG amplitude at the time of stimulation and was EXPRESSED IN UNITS OF average background EMG'. The second endpoint appears twice - as the subtrahend and as the unit. — strength of the relation: 0.9 — the measurement unit was chosen because the animal's reflex form is too variable for the obvious measure
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Up-conditioning of the soleus H-reflex enlarged the right soleus locomotor burst and abolished the right/left step-cycle asymmetry caused by the spinal lesion, whereas the asymmetry persisted in unconditioned control rats.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Transection of the right lateral column left overall walking ability intact but shortened the right stance phase, so that the right-to-left burst-onset time was only 77% of the left-to-right time.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The conditioning protocol roughly doubled the size of the conditioning H-reflex while leaving background EMG and the direct muscle (M) response unchanged, showing the change was reflex-specific rather than a general increase in muscle activation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In conditioned rats the locomotor H-reflexes and the right soleus burst amplitude and width all grew significantly between the first and second treadmill sessions, while control rats showed no significant change.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The correction of asymmetry occurred without any change in the duration (or, since treadmill speed was fixed, the length) of the step cycle in either group.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In uninjured rats the same up- or down-conditioning leaves right/left step symmetry untouched, so the locomotor effect reported here is specific to animals that already have an asymmetry.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
